correctness.rationale: For G=K_{q,q,q,q}, a nonempty set globally dominates G and its complement exactly when it intersects each of four parts. Hence coalition partners have supports whose union is [4], while each valid class has nonempty proper support. The published t-class lower construction realizes 2q, 3q−3, or 4q−8 as feasible, with q=1 boundary K4=2. In the upper proof, t=#distinct singleton-supported part indices. At t=0 counting ≥2 incidences gives k≤2q; at t=1 complementary triple and another incident class force 2z+2≤3q (or k≤2q if no such class); at t=2 compulsory triples and required opposite partner yield k≤3q−3; t=3 entails three excess incidences, k≤3q−3; t=4 entails eight excess, k≤4q−8. Thus the maximum holds for every positive integer q. A fresh direct partition enumeration on original graph and complement gives GC(K4)=2, GC(K2,2,2,2)=4. The all-q statement rests on complete support-incidence inequalities, not finite enumeration.
residual_risks: Revised v4 primary source full text could not be accessed, which affects priority, not the independent combinatorial inequalities.

evidence: The source publishes general multipartite lower construction and exact cases through three parts, and explicitly conjectures sharpness in broader multipartite cases.

value.rationale: This is a natural infinite four-part balanced test of a named multipartite global-coalition conjecture beyond the known three-part exact case. The proof explains three sharp regimes and can inform unrestricted part sizes through compulsory complementary support classes. The new contribution is the upper bound; the lower bound is credited prior work.
residual_risks: It does not solve arbitrary unbalanced complete multipartite graphs or count maximizing partitions.

limitations: Balanced four-part only, not general Conjecture 54; full revised original paper unavailable (vpn_disconnected) and remains explicit originality risk.
